Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And these are the ordinances which you shall recite to them.
translations.2: Say to them: If you purchase a Hebrew slave, he shall serve you six years; and in the seventh, he shall go out free, without payment.
translations.3: If he entered single, he shall go out single; and if he was possessed of a wife, his wife shall go out with him.
translations.4: And if his master gave him a woman in marriage, and she bore him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to his master, and he shall go out single.
translations.5: And if the slave says: I have come to love my master, and my wife and my children — I will not go out free,
translations.6: then his master shall bring him before the judge, and shall bring him to the door-leaf and to the doorposts, and shall mark his ear with a branding iron, and he shall serve him forever.
translations.7: And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant, she shall not go out as the going-out of the male slaves.
translations.8: If she is displeasing to her master, who had intended to marry her, he shall redeem her; he has no power to sell her to some other person who is a stranger to her, since he has been faithless to her.
translations.9: And if he betroths her to his son, he shall deal with her according to the custom due to daughters.
translations.10: And if he marries another, her food, her clothing, and her appointed times he shall not diminish.
translations.11: And if he does not do for her one of these three things, then she shall go out without payment, without price.
translations.12: And whoever strikes a person and kills him shall be put to death.
translations.13: But if he did not intend it — rather God brought it about in His decree — I shall designate for you a place to which he may flee.
translations.14: And if a man acts presumptuously against his fellow and kills him by stealth — even from beside My altar take him and put him to death.
translations.15: And whoever strikes his father or his mother shall be put to death.
translations.16: And whoever kidnaps a person from the sons of Israel and sells him, or is found with him in his possession, shall be put to death.
translations.17: And whoever curses his father or his mother shall be put to death.
translations.18: And when people quarrel, and one of them strikes his fellow with a stone or with a wounding object, and he does not die but takes to his bed,
translations.19: if he rises and walks about in the market on his own supports, then the one who struck him is acquitted — except for his loss of work, which he shall give him, and for medical treatment he shall treat him.
translations.20: And if a person strikes his slave or his maidservant with a rod, and he dies under his hand, he shall be penalized for him.
translations.21: But if he survives a day or two days, he shall not be penalized for him, for he is his property.
translations.22: And if people struggle and they strike a pregnant woman and her child comes out, and there is no fatality, the one who struck her shall be fined as her husband requires of him, and he shall give it by fair assessment.
translations.23: But if there is a fatality, then impose a life in place of a life,
translations.24: and the blood-price of an eye in place of an eye, and a tooth in place of a tooth, and a hand in place of a hand, and a foot in place of a foot,
translations.25: and a burn in place of a burn, and a gash in place of a gash, and a wound in place of a wound.
translations.26: And if a person strikes the eye of his slave or the eye of his maidservant and destroys it, he shall set him free as a free person in place of his eye.
translations.27: And if he knocks out the tooth of his slave or the tooth of his maidservant, he shall set him free as a free person in place of his tooth.
translations.28: And if an ox gores a man or a woman and kills him, the ox shall be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox is clear.
translations.29: But if the ox was a habitual gorer from yesterday and the day before, and its owner was warned but did not guard it, and it kills a man or a woman — the ox shall be stoned and its owner shall also be put to death.
translations.30: If a blood-price is imposed upon him, he shall give the redemption of his life — all that is imposed upon him.
translations.31: And if it gores a son or a daughter, the same ordinance shall be done to it.
translations.32: If the ox gores a slave or a maidservant, he shall give their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
translations.33: And if a person uncovers a pit, or digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
translations.34: the owner of the pit shall pay its price and restore it to its owner, and the dead animal shall be his.
translations.35: And if one man's ox strikes his fellow's ox and it dies, they shall sell the living ox and divide its price, and the dead one they shall also divide.
translations.36: But if it was known that it was a habitual gorer from yesterday and the day before, and its owner did not guard it, he shall deliver an ox in place of his ox, and the dead one shall be his.
translations.37: And if a person steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he shall deliver five in place of the ox, and four in place of the sheep.
